translations.text: Christ,
There was a large village at the head of the great river called the Mtkvari, in a valley called Kola.
Most of the people of that village were pagans who served idols, and the smaller part were Christians who served God.
The children of the Christians and the children of the pagans would gather to play, as children usually do, and they played every day.
In the evening the priest would ring the bell, and the Christian children would go to the church to pray, as is the custom of Christians.
But nine of the pagan children would follow behind them, because they had grown attached to the Christian children and loved the Christian faith.
When they reached the church doors, the Christians would not let them into the church. Instead they said to them:
"You are the children of idol-worshippers, and it is not right for you to come into the house of God."
And they would go away downcast and ashamed. This was done to those children many times.
And after this those youths of the pagans went to the church of the Christians and wished to enter with them, pressing to be let in by force. Then the Christians said to them:
"If you wish to come into the church with us, believe in our Lord Jesus Christ and be baptized in his name, and partake of his mysteries, and join yourselves to the Christians."
They at once accepted this teaching of the Christians with joy and promised to do it.
So the Christians quickly went to the priest who was the presbyter of that village, a holy, worthy and honorable man, and told him about the children.
He remembered the saying of the Gospel spoken by our Lord Jesus Christ:
"Whoever does not leave his father and his mother, his sisters and brothers, his wife and children, and does not take up his cross and follow me, is not worthy of me."
Then that priest went to the bank of the great river, and a crowd of Christians went with him.
The pagan children were also with them. It was winter, and a night of frost,
because he did not dare to baptize them by day for fear of the pagans; and our Lord Jesus Christ was also baptized by John at night in the river Jordan.
At that time the water was bitterly cold.
The children went down into the river, and the priest baptized them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and he sang this hymn:
"The Holy Spirit came down like a dove upon the Jordan when Christ was being baptized; angels stood by and sang this hymn:
Alleluia, alleluia." Then the water became very warm, like a bath,
and by God's command angels brought white garments down from heaven and clothed the newly baptized children with them, unseen by people.
The Christian children became their godparents. They did not return the newly baptized children to their parents. Instead, the children stayed with the Christians and lived with them.
Some time later their parents learned of this matter, and they seized the children by force from the houses of the Christians with great abuse and anger,
with fury and cursing. They took them to their own house, cracked their heads, and covered their bodies with sores by harsh beating.
But the children gave their parents only this answer: "We are Christians, and it is not right for us to eat and drink what has been offered to idols."
The children spent seven days without eating or drinking and tasted nothing at all. Instead they were nourished by the Holy Spirit, whom they had put on at their baptism.
Then their parents promised them every good thing and garments of many colours, but the children kept saying the same words:
"We are Christians and want nothing from you; just let us go, and we will go away with the Christians."
And when they could not overcome their firm faith, they went before the ruler of that time, for he too was a pagan, and told him everything that had happened and the matter of those youths.
And the ruler said to them: "They are your children; you have authority over them. Do with them whatever you wish." And they said to him:
"Give the order and come with us, and let us smash their heads with stones, so that others will not copy them and become Christians."
They also brought no small affliction on the priest: they plundered all his produce and divided up his property among themselves.
They dealt him severe wounds, so that they very nearly killed him, and they drove him out of his home.
Then they set the day for the contest of the holy martyrs.
The ruler came out, and with him a countless crowd of people, and they came to the head of the spring where the holy children had been baptized.
They dug a very deep pit, and the parents brought the holy children and threw them into the pit.
Some of the children were nine years old and some seven, or a little older or younger.
They knew nothing else to say and said only this: "We are Christians, and we will perish and die for him in whom we were baptized."
Then their godless parents smashed their heads and stoned them.
Serpents and vipers, asps and wild beasts know how to show mercy to their young, but these lawless people showed no mercy to their own children.
The crowd of people heaped up stones until they filled the pit and covered the holy bodies with stones, and they poured the earth that had been dug out over them.
And that place became for them a burial place and a martyr's shrine for their holy relics. Then the word of the Gospel was fulfilled:
"Brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child, and parents will rise up against their children and kill them."
Their martyrdom was completed, and they were counted among the first martyrs. With them they rejoice in the kingdom of heaven, wearing crowns, before our Lord Jesus Christ,
to whom belong glory, honour, and worship, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and always and for ever and ever. Amen.
